Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

What we integrate with

Examples of systems commonly found in automotive. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

  • Dealer management system (DMS)

    Source of truth for enquiries, bookings, invoices, job cards, parts and service history. We read and write through its APIs or approved exports, with the OEM's approval where the OEM controls the DMS.

    • OEM-mandated DMS
    • Keyloop or CDK in international groups
    • Multi-brand DMS for independent groups

  • OEM portals and vehicle data

    OEM-owned systems for leads, allocations, warranty and vehicle data. We follow each OEM's data-sharing terms and use only the exports or interfaces the OEM permits.

    • OEM lead management portal
    • Allocation and dispatch portal
    • Warranty and goodwill portal
    • Connected-vehicle data the OEM shares

  • Marketplaces and listing channels

    Lead sources and channels for used-vehicle listings. We connect through the dealer feeds, APIs or bulk uploads each channel offers, prepare listings for manual posting where a channel offers none, and never scrape.

    • CarDekho and CarWale dealer panels
    • BikeDekho and BikeWale
    • OLX listings
    • Google Business Profile

  • Government transport and scheme portals

    Where registration, ownership transfer, NOCs and EV incentive e-vouchers are filed by authorized dealership staff. Our trackers record status and remind owners; they never submit on their own.

    • Vahan
    • Parivahan Sewa
    • PM E-DRIVE portal
    • e-Challan

  • Finance, insurance and warranty

    Where credit decisions, policy issuance and warranty registrations happen. We pass consented referrals and track status; lenders and insurers keep their own disclosures and decisions.

    • Lender DSA or sourcing portals
    • Insurer or MISP sponsor portals
    • OEM extended warranty portals

  • Workshop and field tools

    Bay scheduling, pick-up and drop runs, inspections and payments, connected to the DMS so the job card stays the single record.

    • Workshop management software
    • Driver or field-service app
    • Inspection apps
    • Payment gateway and UPI links

  • Messaging and telephony

    Customer channels with their own rules: opt-in and approved templates for WhatsApp, registered headers and templates for SMS, and preference checks for calls.

    • WhatsApp Business Platform via a provider
    • DLT-registered SMS gateway
    • IVR or cloud telephony

The measures we propose to track

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

Lead first response time
Elapsed time from a lead's arrival in any source to the first meaningful reply or logged call, reported by source, branch and staffed versus unstaffed hours.Why it matters: Slow replies send buyers to the next dealership, and the split shows whether staffing or routing needs work.
Lead-to-test-drive rate
Share of qualified leads in a period that complete a test drive or test ride, by source and model.Why it matters: Shows which sources and follow-up habits produce serious buyers, not just lead volume.
Test-drive-to-booking conversion
Share of completed test drives followed by a booking within the agreed window, by consultant and model.Why it matters: Separates showroom and consultant performance from lead quality.
Booking-to-delivery cycle time
Median days from booking receipt to handover, split into waiting for allotment and time spent on dealer-side milestones such as finance, insurance and registration.Why it matters: Distinguishes OEM supply delays from delays the dealership can fix itself.
Booking cancellation rate
Share of bookings in a period canceled before delivery, with the recorded reason.Why it matters: Shows whether waiting-period communication and finance follow-up are keeping buyers.
Ownership transfer completion time
Days from a used-vehicle sale to the new RC issued in the buyer's name, with files past the statutory reporting window shown separately.Why it matters: Slow transfers leave liability unclear and are a frequent source of post-sale complaints.
Service retention within due window
Share of vehicles due for periodic service in a period that return to the workshop within the agreed window, by model and vehicle age.Why it matters: The core aftersales measure that usage-based reminders and easy booking are meant to improve.
Additional-work approval turnaround
Median time from the technician's recorded finding to the owner's recorded approval or decline.Why it matters: Long waits block bays and push delivery times, and recorded approvals reduce billing disputes.
Repeat repair rate
Share of jobs where the vehicle returns with the same concern within the agreed period.Why it matters: A workmanship and diagnosis measure that matters more to owners than survey scores.
Service recovery closure time
Time from a low rating or complaint to a recorded call-back and outcome.Why it matters: Shows whether feedback leads to action before owners move elsewhere or post a review.

How we connect systems responsibly

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
